summary: All 8 acceptance criteria verified independently against source code.

AC1: No 'failure' key in any AJAX call — all five $.ajax() calls (SetFlag, SavePosition, ToggleBookmark, ToggleImageBookmark, UseAsCover) use the 'error' shorthand (lines 76, 172, 208, 248, 283 of js/viewer.js).
AC2: ShowJumpToModal() uses bootstrap.Modal.getOrCreateInstance() at viewer.js line 139.
AC3: JumpTo() (lines 105–136) contains no 'const viewer = this;' alias. The alias on line 63 belongs to SetFlag() where it is still needed and correct.
AC4: All three $('#btn-jump-go') references in JumpTo() are confirmed (disable on entry: line 113; re-enable on non-success: line 127; re-enable on error: line 132).
AC5: Go button in ReaderPage.php modal footer has id="btn-jump-go" (line 377).
AC6: $currentPageNumber fallback is 1 (line 285 of ReaderPage.php).
AC7/AC8: PHPStan 0 errors, PHPUnit 60/60 confirmed by last terminal run (exit code 0).

comments.note: JumpTo() uses unquoted shorthand method syntax for 'success' and 'error' keys (no quotes), while the rest of the class quotes all AJAX keys ('success', 'error'). Both are valid JS; minor style inconsistency only.
The $('#btn-jump-go') selector appears 3 times in JumpTo(). A cached variable at the top of JumpTo() would be marginally cleaner, but the current scope is small enough that this is negligible.

ShowJumpToModal() calls document.getElementById() directly while the rest of the class uses jQuery. Minor stylistic inconsistency; functionally required for bootstrap.Modal.getOrCreateInstance() which takes an HTMLElement.

The Go button (id=btn-jump-go) lives outside the <form> in the modal footer and is attached via onclick; the form itself handles Enter via onsubmit. This split is correct but worth noting for future maintainers.
